P1.why: LiB report P1 (5.7 ramp, shared with West Face): belay on flat ledge below a vertical crack
P1.text: Stop on the flat ledge at the foot of the vertical crack, once the ramp steps are behind you.

P2.why: LiB P2 (thin-hands splitter): belay toward trees at far left end of the ledge
P2.text: Walk the ledge left to its far end and belay at the trees there.

P3.why: LiB P3 (5.12a): finishes at a bolted belay, now two bolts
P3.text: Belay at the two-bolt anchor reached after the crux finger crack and knobs.

P4.why: LiB P4 (5.11a): finishes at an anchor on a small ledge; 'above the double crack' not in source, removed
P4.text: Belay at the anchor on the small ledge at the top of the pitch.

P5.why: LiB P5: layback past overhanging flake to a narrow ledge; AAC says party moved right from that ledge
P5.text: Belay on the narrow ledge above the overhanging flake, at the top of the pitch; the new line heads off right from there.

P6.why: Blake post: belay in small alcove just right of a razor-sharp flake on the 5.12-/5.11c pitch; 'chimney' not stated, removed
P6.text: Belay in a small alcove just to the right of the sharp flake.

1.why: MP P1: belay at pin and gear anchor below roof, end of long left-facing corner
1.text: Belay below the roof that cuts back left, at the top of the long left-facing corner, on pins and gear.

3.why: MP names no belay for P3, only that the pitch ends at the treed ledge

5.why: MP P5: belay on bolts at end of the traverse into the largest cave
5.text: Belay in the biggest cave on the wall, at the end of the long horizontal traverse left.

8.why: MP P8: belay at treed ledge with bolts after hollow flakes
8.text: Belay at the bolted anchor on the treed ledge reached after the hollow flakes.

1.why: Begg and MP P1: hanging two-bolt belay at top of twin cracks, right crack lieback
1.text: Hang from the two bolts at the top of the twin cracks, up the right-hand crack.

2.why: Begg/MP P2: ledge with bolted anchor at top of offset tips crack with pin
2.text: Belay on the ledge with a bolted anchor, above the offset tips crack and its pin.

3.why: Both P3: gear anchor on large/broad ledge at top of pitch; 'walking left' is the start of pitch, removed
3.text: Belay on the broad ledge at the top of the pitch, building a gear anchor.

4.why: Begg/MP P4: ledge above the pillar with fixed pin and gear (Begg notes it is awkward)
4.text: Belay on the ledge above the pillar, on a fixed pin and gear.

5.why: Begg/MP P5: gear anchor on small ledge past bulge, bolt to the left
5.text: Belay on the small ledge past the bulge, building a gear anchor with a bolt just to the left.

6.why: Begg/MP P6: bolted belay at top of chimney
6.text: Belay at the bolts at the top of the chimney.

1.why: MP P1: bolts beneath second pitch of East Wall route
1.text: Belay at the bolts below the start of the second pitch of the East Wall route.

3.why: MP P3: widening crack to a hanging belay
3.text: Belay hanging at the top of the widening crack.

4.why: MP P4: bolted finish over bulge, belay on a ledge
4.text: Belay on a comfortable ledge after the sport finish over the bulge.

7.why: MP P7: step down around arete to ledge; anchor not for rappelling
7.text: Step down around the corner from the arete to a ledge; its anchor is not meant for rappelling.

8.why: MP P8: belay at bolts just above the lip, or carry on to summit
8.text: Belay at the slackline bolts just over the lip, or go on to the summit.

2.why: MP P2: finish at small ledge with bushy tree
2.text: Belay on the small ledge that has a bushy tree.

3.why: MP P3: angle right past a tree, belay at a horn
3.text: Belay at a horn after angling right past a tree.

4.why: MP P4: around arete onto ledge, blocks, belay by the huge flake
4.text: Belay on blocks next to the huge flake, after the move around the arete onto the ledge.

5.why: MP P5: thin crack, traverse left, ends at spacious ledge
5.text: Finish on the spacious ledge after the traverse left to the second thin crack.

6.why: MP P6: belay at tree below Hercules Tower
6.text: Belay at the tree below the Hercules Tower.

9.why: Sources name a ledge of blocks but no belay; P8 and P9 may be combined

10.why: Sources describe ending at a huge ledge but state no belay
